# The help lists the variable of each option.
$ storectl serve --help
Usage: storectl serve [options]

Run the server of the store.

Options:
      --database-url string  URL of the database.  env DATABASE_URL, key serve.database-url
  -p, --port int             Port to listen on.    default "8080", env STORE_SERVE_PORT, key serve.port
      --workers int          Number of workers.    default "4", env STORE_SERVE_WORKERS, key serve.workers

Global options:
  -c, --config file  Config file in JSON.                                                    env STORE_CONFIG
      --flag-debug   Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env STORE_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help         Show the help.
[exit 0]

# STORE_SERVE_PORT sets the option Port.
$ STORE_SERVE_PORT=9000 storectl serve
serve on port 9000 with 4 workers, database URL unset
[exit 0]

# The program does not read a variable that starts with its name.
$ STORECTL_SERVE_PORT=9000 storectl serve
serve on port 8080 with 4 workers, database URL unset
[exit 0]

# The tag env of DatabaseURL replaces the prefix with the whole variable DATABASE_URL.
$ DATABASE_URL=postgres://store@db/store STORE_SERVE_WORKERS=8 storectl serve --flag-debug
  OPTION          VALUE  SOURCE
  --config        ""     default
  --database-url  ***    env DATABASE_URL
  --port          8080   default
  --workers       8      env STORE_SERVE_WORKERS
serve on port 8080 with 8 workers, database URL set
[exit 0]

# STORE_FLAG_DEBUG turns on the flag --flag-debug.
$ STORE_FLAG_DEBUG=true storectl serve -p 9001
  OPTION          VALUE  SOURCE
  --config        ""     default
  --database-url  ***    default
  --port          9001   flag --port
  --workers       4      default
serve on port 9001 with 4 workers, database URL unset
[exit 0]

$ storectl serve >/dev/full
storectl: main: write the options: clitest: no space left on device
[exit 1]
